note: Language pack for English. Every URL and extraction rule is data — edit here, no recompile. Add a language by creating languages/<Name>/source.json. The 'pronunciation' and 'audio' lists are independent: a site listed for transcriptions need not be listed for recordings, and either list may stand empty. Each list is shown in the order it is written here, whatever order the answers arrive in, so reordering a list reorders the menu. The 'font' block is the typography a headword is drawn in; the 'example' block is the typography example sentences are drawn in; the 'gloss' block is the typography the translations under those example sentences are drawn in, and 'style' may be 'italic' or 'oblique'. Strategies: 'regex' (capture group on body), 'json' (follow dot 'path', then optional 'match'), 'span' (tolerant nested-span IPA reader). 'group' = regex capture group. 'confirm' = regex (with {word}) the body must match. 'normalize' = strip IPA delimiters/entities. 'prefix' = made absolute when the captured address is site-relative. 'varieties' declares the regional varieties this language distinguishes: 'list' rows carry a 'name' and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 'flag', and 'shown' is 'flag' or 'text' (default 'text') for how the UI labels each reading. A pronunciation attempt may replace its flat extraction keys with a 'readings' list; each row carries the same strategy/match/group/path/normalize keys plus 'variety' (a name from the list, or omitted for untagged) and 'skip' (how many earlier matches to pass over, default 0). All readings run on the same fetched body. A flat attempt without 'readings' is one untagged reading. Audio attempts are always flat.

pronunciation.name: Longman
pronunciation.note: Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English. The class is upper-case PRON and the reader is case-sensitive. An unknown word returns a results page with no PRON span, so the attempt simply yields nothing.

pronunciation.name: Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The wikitext attempt reads the {{IPA|en|...}} templates and keys each reading on the accent qualifier, |a=RP for British and |a=US or |a=GA for American. The HTML attempt is the untagged fallback.

pronunciation.name: Cambridge
pronunciation.note: Cambridge prints the British transcription inside the <span class="uk dpron-i"> block and the American one inside <span class="us dpron-i">, each as a nested <span class="ipa">. Each reading's match runs from its block's opening tag to the first ipa span, without crossing into the other block.

pronunciation.name: Oxford
pronunciation.note: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries. The headword British transcription is the first <span class="phon"> and the American one the second, so the American reading skips one match; the page 404s on an unknown word, so no confirm guard is needed.

pronunciation.name: Dictionary.com
pronunciation.note: Dictionary.com prints US and British transcriptions in one <span class="txt-ipa">, comma-separated when a headword has variants, American first. The American reading takes the text before the first comma and the British one the text after it, so a headword without a comma yields American only.

audio.name: Naver
audio.note: Naver English dictionary search API. The audio URL is the opaque, token-bearing 'symbolFile' of the first phonetic symbol (e.g. .../009123.mp3?_lsu_sa_=...). The API returns an empty body without a Referer header, so one is declared here.

audio.name: Longman
audio.note: Longman appends a cache-busting query to each mp3, which the workspace ignores when it names the saved file.

audio.name: Cambridge
audio.note: Cambridge serves per-entry mp3 audio via site-relative <source> src attributes; 'prefix' makes them absolute. The first audio/mpeg source is the headword pronunciation.

audio.name: Oxford
audio.note: Oxford exposes absolute mp3 addresses in data-src-mp3; the first one is the British headword recording.

audio.name: Wiktionary
audio.note: Wiktionary embeds Commons recordings as protocol-relative addresses, so 'prefix' supplies the scheme. Only the transcoded mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is Ogg Vorbis or WAV. The first attempt takes an En- filename, the second a Lingua Libre LL-Q1860_%28eng%29- one, and both prefixes mark the recording as English.
